الزهد هو: الكسب الحلال الذي يكفي له ولأولاده ولمن يعوله، ثم صرف القلب عن الدنيا ومتاعها إلى اللّٰه تعالى، لأن الدنيا مليئة بالشهوات والرغبات، قال اللّٰه تعالى:
﴿زُيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ حُبُّ الشَّهَوَاتِ مِنَ النِّسَاءِ وَالْبَنِينَ وَالْقَنَاطِيرِ الْمُقَنْطَرَةِ مِنَ الذَّهَبِ وَالْفِضَّةِ وَالْخَيْلِ الْمُسَوَّمَةِ وَالْأَنْعَامِ وَالْحَرْثِ ذَٰلِكَ مَتَاعُ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَاللّٰهُ عِنْدَهُ حُسْنُ الْمَآبِ﴾ [سورة آل عمران: ١٤].
وأما ترك السعي للحصول على الرزق، والجلوس في البيت، وانتظار الصدقات والخيرات بحجة التوكل على اللّٰه فهو ليس بزهد، وإنما هو أكل أموال الناس بالباطل باسم الزهد، وكذلك ترك الدنيا وزينتها ليس بزهد، وإنما هو الرهبانية التي أحدثها أهل الكتاب، قال تعالى:
﴿وَرَهْبَانِيَّةً ابْتَدَعُوهَا﴾ [الحديد: ٢٧].
فالفرق بين الزهد المشروع والرهبانية الممنوعة واضح، ولكن لا يدركها إلا أهل العلم والمعرفة، فالزهد بمعنى تزكية النفس عن حب الدنيا وجاهها مطلوب دائمًا وأبدًا لقوله تعالى:
﴿قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَنْ زَكَّاهَا﴾ [الشمس: ٩].
وقد تكون كثرة المال تفيد الأمة في رقيها، وتنمية اقتصادها بما يناسب في عصرها لمقابلة الكفار، فإذا كان المسلم يؤدي حقوقه الواجبة تجاه أمته ودينه، ونفسه لا تغتر بمتاع الدنيا وزخرفها، فالإكثار من المال ليس بمكروه، والأمة الإسلامية منذ عهد النبي ﷺ إلى يومنا هذا قائمة على هذا الأساس.
فإن اللّٰه عز وجل وسع على المسلمين بعد غزو خيبر، فكان النبي ﷺ يدخر لأزواجه قوت سنة كاملة.

collections.intro_en_source:
Asceticism means earning lawful provision sufficient for oneself, one’s children, and those one supports, while turning the heart away from this world and its enjoyments toward Allah, the Exalted. This is because the world is filled with desires and attractions.
Allah, the Exalted, says:
“Beautified for people is the love of desires: women, children, heaped-up treasures of gold and silver, fine horses, livestock, and cultivated land. These are the enjoyments of the worldly life, but with Allah is the best return.”
 [Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:14]
As for abandoning the effort to earn one’s livelihood, sitting at home, and waiting for charity and donations under the claim of relying upon Allah, this is not asceticism. Rather, it is consuming people’s wealth wrongfully in the name of asceticism.
Likewise, completely abandoning the world and its adornments is not asceticism. Rather, that is the monasticism innovated by the People of the Book.
Allah, the Exalted, says:
“And monasticism which they innovated…”
 [Sūrat al-Ḥadīd 57:27]
The distinction between legislated asceticism and prohibited monasticism is clear, although it is properly understood only by people of knowledge and understanding.
Asceticism, in the sense of purifying the soul from attachment to the world and its status, is always sought, as Allah, the Exalted, says:
“Successful indeed is the one who purifies it.”
 [Sūrat al-Shams 91:9]
Possessing abundant wealth may benefit the Ummah by advancing it and strengthening its economy in ways suitable to its time so that it may stand against its enemies.
If a Muslim fulfills the obligatory rights he owes toward his religion and Ummah, while his soul is not deceived by the pleasures and adornments of this world, then possessing much wealth is not disliked.
The Muslim Ummah, from the time of the Prophet ﷺ until today, has operated on this principle.
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, expanded provision for the Muslims after the conquest of Khaybar, and the Prophet ﷺ would store a full year’s provision for his wives.

chapters.intro_ar_source:
رُويَ عن عطية السعدي - وكان من أصحاب النبي ﷺ - قال: قال رسول اللّٰه ﷺ: ((لا يبلغ العبد أن يكون من المتقين حتى يدع ما لا بأس به حذرًا لما به البأس)).
ضعيف: رواه الترمذي (٢٤٥١)، وابن ماجه (٤٢١٥)، والحاكم (٤/٣١٩)، كلهم من طريق أبي عقيل عبد اللّٰه بن عقيل الثقفي، حدثنا عبد اللّٰه بن يزيد، حدثني ربيعة بن يزيد وعطية بن قيس، عن عطية السعدي، فذكره.
قال الترمذي: «هذا حديث غريب لا نعرفه إلا من هذا الوجه».
وقال الحاكم: «هذا حديث صحيح الإسناد ولم يخرجاه».
قال الأعظمي: فيه عبد اللّٰه بن يزيد الدمشقي، ذكره الجوزجاني في أحوال الرجال (٢٩٠) وقال: «أحاديثه منكرة». ولم أقف من تابعه على ذلك، وذكره ابن أبي حاتم في الجرح والتعديل ونقل عن أبيه: «روى عنه أبو عقيل الثقفي ومحمد بن سعد الأنصاري». ولم يقل فيه شيئًا، وذكره ابن حبان في الثقات، ولم أقف على توثيق غيره له، فهو في أكثر أحواله مجهول الحال. ولكن أطلق عليه الحافظ في «التقريب» أنه ضعيف.

It is narrated from ʿAṭiyyah al-Saʿdī—who was among the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ—that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “A servant does not attain the rank of the God-fearing until he leaves what there is no harm in, out of caution regarding what contains harm.”
Weak: Narrated by al-Tirmidhī (2451), Ibn Mājah (4215), and al-Ḥākim (4/319), all through Abū ʿAqīl ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAqīl al-Thaqafī, who narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Yazīd, who narrated from Rabīʿah ibn Yazīd and ʿAṭiyyah ibn Qays, from ʿAṭiyyah al-Saʿdī.
Al-Tirmidhī said: “This is a gharīb hadith; we do not know it except through this route.”
Al-Ḥākim said: “This hadith has an authentic chain of transmission, although al-Bukhārī and Muslim did not narrate it.”
Al-Aʿẓamī said: Its chain contains ʿAbdullāh ibn Yazīd al-Dimashqī. Al-Jūzajānī mentioned him in Aḥwāl al-Rijāl (290) and said, “His hadiths are objectionable.” I did not find anyone who supported him in that judgment. Ibn Abī Ḥātim mentioned him in al-Jarḥ wa-al-Taʿdīl and transmitted from his father: “Abū ʿAqīl al-Thaqafī and Muḥammad ibn Saʿd al-Anṣārī narrated from him,” without giving a judgment on him. Ibn Ḥibbān mentioned him among the trustworthy narrators, and I found no other scholar who explicitly declared him trustworthy. Thus, at best, his status is unknown. Al-Ḥāfiẓ, however, stated plainly in al-Taqrīb that he is weak.

chapters.intro_ar_source:
قال اللّٰه تعالى:
﴿اعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا لَعِبٌ وَلَهْوٌ وَزِينَةٌ وَتَفَاخُرٌ بَيْنَكُمْ وَتَكَاثُرٌ فِي الْأَمْوَالِ وَالْأَوْلَادِ كَمَثَلِ غَيْثٍ أَعْجَبَ الْكُفَّارَ نَبَاتُهُ ثُمَّ يَهِيجُ فَتَرَاهُ مُصْفَرًّا ثُمَّ يَكُونُ حُطَامًا وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ مِنَ اللّٰهِ وَرِضْوَانٌ وَمَا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا إِلَّا مَتَاعُ الْغُرُورِ﴾ [الحديد: ٢٠].
chapters.intro_ar_display:
قال اللّٰه تعالى:
﴿اعْلَمُوا أَنَّمَا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا لَعِبٌ وَلَهْوٌ وَزِينَةٌ وَتَفَاخُرٌ بَيْنَكُمْ وَتَكَاثُرٌ فِي الْأَمْوَالِ وَالْأَوْلَادِ كَمَثَلِ غَيْثٍ أَعْجَبَ الْكُفَّارَ نَبَاتُهُ ثُمَّ يَهِيجُ فَتَرَاهُ مُصْفَرًّا ثُمَّ يَكُونُ حُطَامًا وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ وَمَغْفِرَةٌ مِنَ اللّٰهِ وَرِضْوَانٌ وَمَا الْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا إِلَّا مَتَاعُ الْغُرُورِ﴾ [الحديد: ٢٠].
chapters.intro_en_source:
Allah, the Exalted, says:
“Know that the life of this world is only play, amusement, adornment, boasting among yourselves, and competition in wealth and children. It is like rain whose vegetation pleases the farmers; then it dries, and you see it turn yellow, then it becomes debris. And in the Hereafter there is severe punishment, as well as forgiveness from Allah and His pleasure. The life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion.”
 [Sūrat al-Ḥadīd 57:20]

“Beautified for people is the love of desires: women, children, heaped-up treasures of gold and silver, fine horses, livestock, and cultivated land. These are the enjoyments of worldly life, but with Allah is the best return.”
 [Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:14]

Allah, the Exalted, says:
“Then We sent after them Our messengers, and We sent after them Jesus son of Mary and gave him the Gospel. We placed compassion and mercy in the hearts of those who followed him. But monasticism they invented; We did not prescribe it for them, except that they sought the pleasure of Allah, yet they did not observe it as it should have been observed. So We gave those among them who believed their reward, but many of them are defiantly disobedient.”
 [Sūrat al-Ḥadīd 57:27]
